summary: Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harvard University (B.A. ~1960–1964, M.A. ~1969–1971, Ph.D. ~1971–1974) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–1967), where he later served as professor from ~1976 to 2022.

Michael Weiers was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn (~1960–1965). He served as professor at the University of Bonn (1972–2003) and held an honorary professorship at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies practitioner who earned an M.A. at The New School and trained under Mel Weitsman (~1973–2021). He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center (~1984) and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis, an Indologist and historian-archaeologist, earned his B.A. from the University of Victoria and his doctorate from the University of Chicago (-1988). He served as curator at the British Museum (1994–2014) and held posts at the British Library and Royal Asiatic Society.

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Paul Thieme, Karl Hoffmann, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, Johanna Narten, F. B. J. Kuiper, and Jununath Pandit. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1978–1986) before moving to Harvard University in 1986.
Michael Yorke is a religious studies scholar affiliated with Yale University, where he is also attested as a graduate student in 2026.

Michael Zimmermann is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg (~1993–2000) and studied at Soka University. He served as professor at Stanford University (2003) and became professor and director at the University of Hamburg (~2007).

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Rostock (1968–1973) and the University of Madras (~1980–1985), later holding professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger (attested 2008) and also studied under Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at Komazawa University and earned her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (-2014). She held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Göttingen, and became an assistant professor at Stanford University in 2016.

Michaël Peyrot is a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at Leiden University (1999–2010), later holding posts there (~2008, 2016) and at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bitbol is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University (-1985) under Pierre Mills. He held positions at CNRS (~1997, emeritus 2020), University of Paris, Linacre College, IHPST, University of Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne, and École Normale Supérieure.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1852–1855) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1857–1860) under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as a professor at the Collège de France (1864–1905) and director at EPHE (1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his studies and doctoral thesis at the University of South Africa (~1989–1999). He also held an academic post at the University of South Africa starting in 1990.

Michel Hulin was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1978) under Olivier Lacombe. He served as a faculty member at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988. He served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from ~1990 to 2012.
Michel Ledrus was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He held appointments at KU Leuven (1931), the Pontifical Gregorian University (1932–1933), and Collegio Bellarmino (1949).

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet (~1928–1935). He held faculty posts at the University of Poitiers (~1933–1938), EPHE (~1938–1977), and the University of Paris (~1947–1977).

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida, later holding posts at Geneva (1987–1992), Hanazono University (2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2007).

Michel Soymié was a sinologist and scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at INALCO (~1948–1952). He held posts at CNRS (1951–1956), EFEO (~1952–1966), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1957–1960), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1966–1992).
